clue.text: Pressure, say, gutted a revolutionary spirit

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for pressure in physics

indicators.note: a gutted word has lost its insides, so only its outer letters remain

parts.note: Che Guevara is the crossword's favourite revolutionary

explanation.surface: Someone under pressure, it seems, has had the spirit knocked out of a political firebrand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' empties SAY to SY, which sits between P and CHE.
explanation.definitionFit: The psyche is the human soul or mind, the inner spirit of a person.

clue.text: Force and twist top off vermouth?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for force in physics

indicators.note: with its top taken off, the word for twist loses its first letter

parts.note: to twist something violently is to wrench it

explanation.surface: A bartender twists the cap off a vermouth bottle with some force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top off' removes the W of WRENCH, leaving RENCH after F. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: French is a type of dry vermouth, as in the cocktail order 'gin and French'.

clue.text: Constrain temperature during bad weather? Assuredly

parts.note: to constrain someone is to force them

indicators.note: the temperature falls during the bad weather, so its letter goes inside that word

parts.note: rain is the classic British bad weather

explanation.surface: A forecaster is asked whether the cold will be held in check by the storm, and answers confidently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts T inside RAIN, making RTAIN after FORCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To know something for certain is to know it surely and without doubt.

clue.text: Member's central point: Member's not working with Government

parts.note: M abbreviates Member, as in MP or MBE; the 's reads as 'is' joining the pieces
someone not working is idle

explanation.surface: An MP's main argument is that a colleague is lazy and doing nothing alongside the Government.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Member' is a leg, the body part, not an MP.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg is a limb, and the middle of a limb is the midpoint of that leg.

clue.text: Mountaineers, supple, in Caucasus on vacation

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
a word on vacation is emptied of its middle, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: a supple body is limber

explanation.surface: Fit, supple mountaineers are holidaying in the Caucasus range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties CAUCASUS to CS, and LIMBER goes inside it ('in').
explanation.definitionFit: Mountaineers ascend peaks, so they are climbers by activity.

clue.text: Spot reduced description of work

indicators.note: a reduced word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a speck is a tiny spot

explanation.surface: A short job specification is easy to spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' drops the K from SPECK.
explanation.definitionFit: A spec is short for specification, a detailed account of a job to be done.

clue.text: Minister, not well in middle of week, getting wake-up call

parts.note: a minister of religion is addressed as Rev, short for Reverend

indicators.note: the illness sits in the middle of the week, so its letters go inside
the middle of a word is its central letters

parts.note: someone not well is ill

explanation.surface: A clergyman, ill midweek, gets an early-morning call to rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes EE from WEEK, and 'in' puts ILL between those letters, giving EILLE after REV.
explanation.definitionFit: Reveille is the bugle signal that rouses soldiers in the morning.

clue.text: Bloke's accommodating ailing pony's sleepy state

indicators.note: accommodating means holding something within, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: a bloke is a man, so bloke's means his

indicators.note: an ailing thing is out of sorts, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A man is giving shelter to his sick pony, which has become drowsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ailing' turns PONYS into YPNOS, and 'accommodating' puts that inside HIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypnosis is a trance-like condition resembling sleep.

clue.text: A lot of skill embraced by tailors at work may be this

definitions.text: A lot of skill embraced by tailors at work may be this

indicators.note: the skill is held inside the other letters
letters at work are busy being rearranged
a lot of a word, though not all, means it loses its last letter

parts.note: art is skill or craft

explanation.surface: Tailors busy at their craft show plenty of skill, and the result is to do with clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' cuts ART to AR; 'at work' turns TAILORS into STORIAL; 'embraced by' puts AR inside: S-AR-TORIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Sartorial means relating to tailoring and dress, so tailors' skill is sartorial skill.

clue.text: What a shame about the end of wholesome devotion

indicators.note: the regret goes about the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: 'What a pity!' says the same as 'What a shame!'

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone sighs that it is a pity that healthy, wholesome devotion has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts PITY around E, the last letter of 'wholesome'.
explanation.definitionFit: Piety is religious devoutness, a reverent devotion.

clue.text: Caught one between American locations turning pessimistic

indicators.note: turning sends the whole string back to front
the caught one sits between the two places, so it goes inside them

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles and NYC is New York City
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A traveller caught between two US cities grows gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' puts CI between LA and NYC, giving LACINYC; 'turning' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Cynical describes someone distrustful who expects the worst of people, close to pessimistic.

clue.text: Spy, old woman, showing nothing incriminating

parts.note: ma is mother, informally the 'old woman'
a suspect with nothing incriminating on them is clean

explanation.surface: An elderly woman suspected of spying turns out to have nothing incriminating on her.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Maclean was one of the Cambridge Five who passed secrets to the Soviet Union.

clue.text: Appliance there bottles volatile liquid

indicators.note: the words hold the answer inside them as a bottle holds liquid

explanation.surface: A household appliance stores a volatile liquid in bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across 'appliancE THERe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether is a highly volatile, flammable solvent once used as an anaesthetic.

clue.text: Appalling ill-usage limiting second of army fighters

indicators.note: limiting means bounding, so the other letters close round it
appalling treatment is all wrong, so these letters are reshuffled
the second of a word is its second letter

explanation.surface: Irregular fighters are subjected to terrible abuse that hems in a regular army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appalling' rearranges ILLUSAGE as GUEILLAS, and 'limiting' wraps it round R, the second letter of 'army'.
explanation.definitionFit: Guerillas are irregular soldiers fighting in small independent bands.

clue.text: Source of food decoration using garlic improbably left unadopted

indicators.note: the leftover letters are arranged in an unlikely way, scrambling them
the left letter is not taken up, so it is removed from the words

explanation.surface: A cook absurdly decorates food with garlic, then abandons the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unadopted' removes L from USING GARLIC; 'improbably' rearranges the ten letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing sugar is the fine powdered sugar used to make icing for cakes.

clue.text: Project to secure site of battle

parts.note: to project is to jut out
to secure a prize or deal is to land it

explanation.surface: A military planner's project is to capture a battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Project' reads as a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Jutland, in 1916, was the great naval clash of the First World War.

clue.text: Quantity of champagne? In France I travel, carrying one-third of bottle

parts.note: je is French for I

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: to roam is to travel about

indicators.note: one-third of a six-letter word is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A traveller in France carries part of a bottle of fizz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one-third of' takes BO from BOTTLE, and 'carrying' puts it inside ROAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeroboam is a large champagne bottle holding four standard bottles, so a measure of it.

clue.text: Impertinence, being still upset about excellence

indicators.note: the turned word goes about the other, enclosing it
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: still in the sense 'yet', as in 'still to come'
merit is worth or excellence

explanation.surface: A person's continued cheek is upsetting someone despite their quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns YET into TEY, and 'about' wraps that round MERIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Temerity is reckless boldness or audacity, a near synonym for cheek.

clue.text: Healthful water filling trench? Hurry

indicators.note: the water fills the trench, so it goes inside

parts.note: a ditch is a trench
a spa is a spring of mineral water thought healthful

explanation.surface: Mineral water fills a trench and someone rushes about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispatch means speed or haste, as in 'with all dispatch'.

clue.text: People with guns? People with scissors have less power

indicators.note: having less means one letter is lost

parts.note: snippers are people who snip with scissors

explanation.surface: Gunmen and scissor-wielders compared, the latter less powerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Snipers shoot from hiding, so they are people with guns.

clue.text: Recall I'm sincere when pressured?

indicators.note: letters under pressure get squashed out of shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone under interrogation insists they are sincere about what they remember.
explanation.definitionFit: To reminisce is to recall past events fondly.

clue.text: Engage in digging up river to confine smell

indicators.note: confining one word means holding it inside another

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A dig beside a river turns up a smell that must be contained.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhume is to dig up something buried, especially a body.

clue.text: Category of ecological interest about to be moved to the back

indicators.text: to be moved to the back
indicators.note: the about letters are shifted from the front part to the end

parts.note: green means environmental, so it denotes ecological interest
re is Latin for about, concerning

explanation.surface: Environmental matters are to be relegated to the back of the agenda.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a kind or class, especially of art or literature.

clue.text: Endlessly fix promotional material showing beautiful females

indicators.note: a word endlessly given loses its last letter

parts.note: to nail something is to fix it in place
ads are advertisements, promotional material

explanation.surface: Someone constantly patches up advertising that features attractive women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts NAIL to NAI.
explanation.definitionFit: Naiads are water nymphs of Greek myth, usually pictured as lovely young women.

clue.text: European assembly not against exit

indicators.note: not means without, so the against letters are removed

parts.note: a congress is a formal assembly
con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A European assembly that is not opposed votes to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Egress is a way out, the formal word for exit.

clue.text: Drink supplier refuses to accept expression of thanks about one

indicators.note: the refusals accept one, taking it in among their letters
the refusals also sit about the one, enclosing it

parts.note: to bar is to refuse entry, so refuses means bars
I is the Roman numeral one
ta is British slang for thank you

explanation.surface: A server will not accept thanks for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuses to accept expression of thanks' reads as one phrase, but 'to accept' and 'about' both put BARS round I; TA, British slang for thanks, follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A barista makes and serves coffee drinks in a café.

clue.text: Active article expelled by aerosol

indicators.note: the article is thrown out of the aerosol, so its letter is removed

parts.note: an aerosol is a spray
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An active item is ejected by an aerosol can.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry means lively and nimble, especially of an older person.

clue.text: Freight expert getting gold to position within hour

indicators.note: within means inside, so these letters go into the hour

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
the lie of something is its position

explanation.surface: A freight specialist gets bullion into place within the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A haulier runs a business transporting goods by road.

clue.text: Eighteen letters about college player

indicators.note: the eighteen letters go about the college, enclosing it

parts.note: A to R spans the first eighteen letters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A student performer has eighteen letters to write about their college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eighteen letters' are not a count but the range A TO R.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor plays a role, so a player in the theatrical sense.

clue.text: Fellow in committee with computer software for soldiers

indicators.note: the fellow sits in the committee-with-software string, so goes inside it

parts.note: DOS is a computer operating system, a piece of software
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A man on a committee brings software for the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts MAN inside COM plus DOS, splitting them: COM-MAN-DOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Commandos are soldiers trained for raids.
